title: Vadose Zone Analytical Algorithm Assessment, Conservation Repair & SWAP5 Suitability

primary_source.citation: Sadeghi et al. (2026), Vadose zone analytical algorithm (VZAA): a non-iterative algorithm for vadose zone soil moisture and groundwater recharge, Journal of Hydrology 673, 135467

reason: published complete method reports non-zero accepted profile mass-balance residuals
published formulation cannot strictly impose a general lower prescribed-head or prescribed-flux boundary
published layered-soil case degrades because the analytical flux relation was derived for uniform soil
literal half-order history grows with the complete time history and does not satisfy compact persistent state or strong predictable-cost requirements

donor_extraction.candidate: isolate the transient diffusive/history flux estimator and test as predictor or diagnostic inside an exactly conservative common/LayeredMFP-compatible harness
donor_extraction.acceptance_rule: raw VZAA prediction may never become committed transfer without exact conservative acceptance semantics

conservative_derivative.required_proof: Demonstrate a materially distinct benefit over LayeredMFP or other common reduced-order machinery before a separate solver family is justified. Exact accepted-step ledger, explicit bottom interface and bounded correction count remain mandatory.

compressed_fractional_history.required_proof: Error, restart, rollback, conservation interaction and performance must be qualified independently.

next_actions: capture and provenance-check DOI-linked supplementary MATLAB appendices
reproduce a fixed-domain case and test Eq. 8 telescoping to roundoff
decompose moving-water-table residual into unsaturated storage, saturated storage, geometry crossing, clipping and lower-boundary terms
identify the actual Eq. 9 local solution method and count function evaluations
isolate the VZAA transient diffusive/history term as a donor candidate
design an isolated donor A/B against current LayeredMFP and FullRichards without changing production code
reject standalone derivative work unless a distinct accuracy/applicability advantage is demonstrated
